title: Hot, acidic KMnO₄: how it attaches and how it cleaves
intent: After this scene the learner can say: "MnO₄⁻ first bonds to both alkene carbons from one face, as in the cold reaction, and water gives the diol. Hot and acidic, KMnO₄ keeps going: the bond that joined the two OH carbons is cut and each end becomes C=O. An end with no H stays a ketone; an end with one H goes on to a carboxylic acid; =CH₂ goes to CO₂."

products.name: acetone (propan-2-one)
products.note: From the (CH₃)₂C= end: no H on that carbon, so it stops at the ketone.

products.name: acetic acid (ethanoic acid)
products.note: From the =CH(CH₃) end: its H lets the aldehyde be oxidised on to the acid.

products.name: 2-methylbutane-2,3-diol
products.note: Where cold, dilute, basic KMnO₄ stops (beat 4). One stereocentre (C3 of the diol); both faces react equally, so a racemate. Not cis/trans or meso: C2 of the diol carries two CH₃.

intermediates.name: manganate(VII) monoester of the diol (a course-level simplification)

beats.caption: 2-Methylbut-2-ene meets hot, acidic KMnO₄. Permanganate is purple; its Mn(VII) badly wants electrons.
beats.captionOrbitals: The π cloud of the C=C sits above and below the flat molecule: a top face and a bottom face.

beats.caption: Two O atoms of MnO₄⁻ line up over the top face of the C=C, one above each carbon.
beats.captionOrbitals: The top half of the π cloud reaches up toward the two O atoms waiting above it.
beats.notes: MnO₄⁻ is stood upright over the C=C (place move in the frame C1→C2): O(a) above C1, O(b) above C2, Mn above the middle and its other two O further up, so the ring of b3 reads as a pentagon on the top face.

beats.caption: In one step both C–O bonds form, both on the top face (syn): a cyclic manganate ester. Mn(VII) → Mn(V).

arrows.why: The π pair forms a bond from C1 to one oxo O, on the top face.
That Mn=O π pair moves onto Mn: Mn gains two electrons (Mn(VII) → Mn(V)).
A second Mn=O π pair forms the bond from O to C2, on the same face.

beats.notes: No ring glyph: the five-membered ring is drawn with ordinary bonds only (readability pass 2026-10-21; a filled ring sat over the Mn and O labels on a phone).

beats.caption: Water cuts the two O–Mn bonds, never the C–O bonds: the diol. Cold, dilute, basic KMnO₄ stops here.
beats.notes: Summary beat, as scene 06 b5: no arrows (hydrolysis detail is beyond the course). The Mn fragment (9, 10, 11) fades out while an H fades in on O7 and on O8 (explicit, because the O7–H bond is an arrow source in b6). C1–O7 and C2–O8 never break. Under cold, dilute, basic conditions the reaction stops here (scene 06).

beats.caption: Hot and acidic, it goes on: a fresh MnO₄⁻ bonds to one OH oxygen, and HO⁻ leaves. Mn(VII) wants a pair.
beats.notes: Summary beat: a simplified attachment (the O–H of one OH swapped for O–Mn; the HO⁻ is water in the acid). Beyond the course: how permanganate really attacks the diol is not taught, and hot-acid cleavage need not go through the free diol at all.

beats.caption: The bond that joined the two OH carbons is cut. Each end becomes C=O, and Mn takes the pair: Mn(V).

arrows.why: The C–C σ pair swings onto C2 and its O: it becomes the C2=O bond. The two halves come apart.
The O–Mn pair moves onto Mn, so Mn gains two electrons: Mn(VII) → Mn(V).
The O–H pair on the other carbon becomes its C1=O bond; the H leaves as H⁺.

beats.notes: Course level (McMurry Fundamentals: hot or acidic KMnO₄ cleaves the C=C, each end becoming C=O): one concerted picture of the cut, drawn the way the course says it, 'the bond that joined the two OH carbons is cut; each end becomes C=O'. The real hot-acid mechanism is beyond the course.

beats.caption: Sort the ends. The (CH₃)₂C end has no H: a ketone, acetone. The CH end still has an H: an aldehyde.
KMnO₄ oxidises that C–H too: the aldehyde becomes acetic acid. Purple MnO₄⁻ ends as brown MnO₂.
beats.notes: Summary beat: the aldehyde → acid oxidation is not drawn with arrows (beyond the course: water adds to the C=O and that hydrate is oxidised). The HO⁻ oxygen becomes the new OH; H⁺ and the manganese fragment fade out.

beats.caption: Acetone and acetic acid, from one C=C. A =CH₂ end would be oxidised all the way to CO₂.

stereoCallout.title: Syn attachment, then the stereocentre is erased
stereoCallout.text: Both O come from one MnO₄⁻ on one face (syn), as in the cold reaction. On this alkene the diol has one stereocentre and forms as a racemate (no cis/trans: one carbon has two CH₃). Cleavage then erases it: acetone and acetic acid have no stereocentres.

options.text: 6-Oxoheptanoic acid, CH₃CO(CH₂)₄CO₂H: the ring opens, one end a ketone, one end an acid.
options.why: Yes. The C=C is cut. The carbon with the CH₃ has no H: ketone. The CH carbon has one H: acid. A ring gives one chain.
That is the cold, dilute, basic product (scene 06). Hot or acidic KMnO₄ does not stop at the diol: it cuts the C=C.

options.text: Two separate molecules: a ketone and a carboxylic acid
options.why: The C=C is inside a ring, so cutting it opens the ring: both new ends stay on one chain, 6-oxoheptanoic acid.
The CH end has an H, so hot KMnO₄ does not stop at the aldehyde: it oxidises it on to CO₂H.

notes: Course level: McMurry Fundamentals Ch 4 (hot or acidic KMnO₄ cleaves a C=C; an end with no H gives a ketone, one H a carboxylic acid, two H CO₂). The scene keeps to that level. One step deeper, and marked as such in the beat notes: the second MnO₄⁻ bonding to the diol (b5), the arrows of the cut (b6) and the aldehyde → acid step (b8) are course-level pictures, not the full mechanism.
Beats 1-3 reuse scene 06 (the one-step syn attachment and the cyclic manganate ester); b4 is scene 06's hydrolysis, where the cold reaction stops.
The hub card example (alkene-kmno4-acid) is the same reaction: CC=C(C)C → CC(C)=O + CC(=O)O. Lesson 10 s14 (the cleave-it task) uses the same alkene.

Stereo: 'so the diol is cis' does not apply to this alkene: 2-methylbutane-2,3-diol has one stereocentre (C2 of the diol carries two CH₃), so it forms as a racemate, not as a cis or meso compound. The callout says so.
Mn oxidation states are badges, not charges. The final MnO₂ is named in the caption only (not drawn).
